morning: Time for coffee and a chat
afternoon: Shall we continue with the lesson?

hero.description: Pop in and get started right now

brain_1.text: Review new words 15 minutes after learning to strengthen neural connections.

sleep_1.text: Sleep after learning transfers information from short-term to long-term memory.

nutrition_1.text: Nuts and blueberries improve concentration during intense study sessions.

hydration_1.text: Even mild dehydration reduces cognitive abilities by 10%.

method_songs.text: Listen to songs in the target language and try to identify words without looking at the lyrics.

practice_aloud.text: Say words out loud. The muscle memory of your speech apparatus helps with retention.

habit_daily.text: 5 minutes every day is better than 2 hours once a week.

assoc_pics.text: Link a word to a funny or weird mental image — it will 'stick' much faster.

handwriting.text: Writing words by hand activates specific brain areas that typing doesn't reach.

walking.text: Walking while memorizing stimulates blood flow to the prefrontal cortex.

funny_story.text: Try to make up a ridiculous story using new words — the brain loves context.

focus_phone.text: Put your phone in another room. Even the sight of a smartphone lowers your cognitive capacity.

spaced_rep.text: Use spaced repetition: 1 day, 3 days, a week, a month.

dopamine.text: Dopamine is fuel for learning. Set micro-goals and praise yourself for achieving them.

chunks.text: Learn ready-made phrases (chunks) instead of just rules. The brain recalls them faster.

scent.text: Associate learning with a specific scent. It will become a powerful memory trigger.

native_role.text: Imagine yourself as a native speaker. Mimicking an accent relaxes the speech center.

do_not_disturb.text: 'Do Not Disturb' mode saves up to 20 minutes of time needed to re-enter a flow state.

dark_chocolate.text: Dark chocolate (70%+ cocoa) briefly improves blood flow to the brain.

cardio.text: Cardio before studying raises BDNF levels, a protein responsible for neuron growth.

color_markers.text: Use different colored markers for different parts of speech to speed up recognition.

feynman_tech.text: Explain a complex topic to an imaginary child. This is the Richard Feynman technique.

pomodoro.text: The Pomodoro Technique (25 min study, 5 min rest) prevents burnout.

white_noise.text: White noise or nature sounds help block out sharp external distractions.

shadowing.text: Shadowing method: repeat after the speaker immediately as you hear the word.

top_1000.text: Learn the top 1000 most frequent words first — they cover 75% of everyday speech.

shower_ideas.text: Insights often come in the shower when the brain enters its default mode network.

mind_maps.text: Draw Mind Maps to visualize connections between different topics.

evening_recall.text: Recall 3 new words at the end of the day to strengthen connections before sleep.

podcasts.text: Listen to podcasts in the background. Even passive listening gets your brain used to the rhythm.

stickers.text: Put stickers with object names on furniture and appliances around your home.

forgetting_curve.text: Forgetting is normal. Active recall is much better than just re-reading.

reading_20.text: Read texts where 20% of words are unfamiliar. This is your 'zone of proximal development'.

deep_breath.text: Taking a deep breath before starting a session oxygenates your brain.

mirror_practice.text: Look in the mirror when practicing the pronunciation of difficult sounds.

multitasking_myth.text: Focus on one task. Multitasking is an illusion that reduces efficiency by 40%.

peak_energy.text: Do your hardest tasks during your peak energy hours (morning bird or night owl).

social_fear.text: Find a conversation partner. The fear of making a mistake in front of a person alerts the brain.

target_subs.text: Watch movies with subtitles in the target language, not your native one.

habit_stacking.text: Attach study to a ritual: e.g., learn 5 words while brushing your teeth.

marginalia.text: Write in the margins of books. A dialogue with the author helps you digest material.

neuroplasticity.text: Believe in neuroplasticity. The brain is capable of changing at any age.

omega_3.text: Omega-3 fatty acids are building blocks for neuron membranes.

comedy.text: Watch comedies in the language. Laughter lowers cortisol levels that hinder learning.

start_small.text: Don't spend months on grammar — start speaking immediately using simple phrases.

ui_language.text: Switch your phone's interface language to the target language.

context_learning.text: Don't learn words in lists. Learn them in sentences to understand how they are used.

gum_flavor.text: Chew a unique flavor of gum only while studying to create a sensory association.

temp_focus.text: The brain works more efficiently in a cool room (18-20°C) than in the heat.

error_data.text: Errors are data, not failure. Every mistake makes your neural network more accurate.

baroque_music.text: Baroque music (classical without words) helps the brain enter an alpha-wave state.

etymology.text: Study etymology. Knowing the root helps you guess the meaning of related words.

fillers.text: Pay attention to filler words used by natives — they make your speech sound natural.

nature_view.text: Looking at plants or taking a walk in the park restores your attention span.

why_goal.text: Define your 'Why?'. Without clear motivation, the prefrontal cortex gives up easily.

voice_recorder.text: Record yourself speaking and listen back — you'll notice errors you usually miss.

micro_steps.text: Break a big topic into tiny pieces. A small step is easier to start.

caffeine_timing.text: Caffeine works best about 20 minutes after consumption. Plan your breaks accordingly.

mind_palace.text: Use the 'Mind Palace' technique — place new concepts in a familiar room.

novelty_loc.text: Change your study spot. A change of scenery forces the brain to be more alert.

silence_pause.text: Sit in silence for 10 minutes after a difficult block of study without any gadgets.

children_books.text: Read children's books. They have simple vocabulary and lots of repetition.

automation.text: Practice basic phrases until they are automatic to save cognitive resources.

absurd_assoc.text: The more absurd the association, the higher the chance the hippocampus will store it.

structure_first.text: Learn the structure of the language first, then build your vocabulary on it.

weekly_sprint.text: Set weekly goals instead of yearly ones. A short horizon is more motivating.

daylight.text: Bright daylight suppresses melatonin and helps you stay awake over your books.

syn_ant_pairs.text: Learn synonyms and antonyms in pairs. The brain loves opposites.

habit_tracker.text: Keep a habit tracker. Seeing your streak of success stimulates you to continue.

protein_breakfast.text: A protein-rich breakfast helps maintain focus longer than a high-carb one.

posture.text: A straight back signals to the brain that the current moment is important.

guess_context.text: Try to guess a word's meaning from context before looking it up in the dictionary.

two_minute_rule.text: The hardest part is the first 2 minutes. Just promise yourself to 'open the book'.

thematic_groups.text: Sort words by themes: kitchen, feelings, work — rather than alphabetically.

echo_lalia.text: Echolalia: mimic the native speaker's intonation, not just their words.

cognates.text: Look for cognates (words that look similar in your language and the target one).

immersion_day.text: Have an 'immersion day' — listen, read, and speak only in the target language for 24 hours.

sleep_learning.text: The brain learns while you sleep. Studying without sleep is like writing on sand.

relevance.text: Don't learn everything. Choose only what you will actually use in real life.

role_play.text: Role-play scenarios: ordering coffee, buying a ticket, meeting someone.

visual_metaphor.text: Explain grammar rules through visual metaphors.

power_nap.text: A power nap (20 min) reloads your working memory.

hobby_link.text: Learn the language through your hobbies. If you love cooking, read recipes.

accent_courage.text: Don't be afraid of your accent. An accent is proof that you know more than one language.

layer_method.text: First focus on meaning, then grammar, then pronunciation.

headphone_focus.text: Study with headphones on, even if nothing is playing.

muscle_skill.text: Language is a muscle, not just knowledge. It needs constant training, not just theory.

personal_mem.text: Connect new words to your personal memories.

thyroid_check.text: Check your thyroid levels if your memory has significantly worsened.

reward_system.text: Create a reward system for yourself for every level you complete.

shopping_list.text: Write your shopping lists in the language you are learning.

culture_code.text: Study the mentality. Many phrases don't make sense without the cultural code.

stress_block.text: High stress blocks Broca's area, the part of the brain responsible for speech.

gamification.text: Use apps with levels and rankings to keep things fun.

intensity.text: Short, deep immersion sessions are more effective than years of casual study.

melatonin.text: Melatonin in the dark helps with memory consolidation.

joy_content.text: Find content you genuinely enjoy and forget that you are actually 'studying'.

triple_link.text: Link a new word to at least three words you already know.

snowball.text: Use the 'snowball' method — add one new word to a phrase you already know.

aesthetics.text: Buy nice stationery. Tactile pleasure increases your desire to study.

multi_channel.text: Synapses strengthen when repeating through different channels: sound, sight, motion.

puzzles.text: Solve language puzzles to activate your brain's search mechanisms.

virtual_walk.text: Virtual walks on Google Maps help you remember names of places.

quality_500.text: It's better to know 500 words perfectly than 2000 with a dictionary.

pre_study_med.text: Meditation before studying clears your brain's 'RAM'.

brainstorm.text: Brainstorming: write down as many words as you can on a topic like 'City' in 1 minute.

workspace_clean.text: Structured chaos is bad. Keep your workspace clean.

difficulty_grad.text: Increase difficulty gradually. Too easy is boring, too hard is scary.

theater_reading.text: Read dialogues with different emotions (angry, happy, whispering).

stupid_risk.text: Don't be afraid to look stupid. It's an inevitable stage of language learning.

verb_motor.text: Verbs are more important than nouns. A verb is the engine of a sentence.

meta_learning.text: Learn how to learn. Understanding your cognitive traits saves years.

water_glass.text: A glass of water nearby is the best way to quickly wake up your brain.

micro_breaks.text: Use 'micro-breaks' — look out the window for 30 seconds after every page read.

flow_state.text: Find a difficulty level where time flies by unnoticed.

news_radio.text: Listen to the news. They have clear diction and standardized vocabulary.

photo_notes.text: Take photos of your notes to review them while in line or on transit.

morning_will.text: Willpower is limited. Study in the morning while your 'battery' is full.

paraphrase.text: Paraphrase your thought if you forget a specific word. This develops fluency.

subject_synth.text: Combine two subjects. For example, study history in English.

vitamin_b.text: B vitamins are critical for the conduction of nerve impulses.

perfectionism_exit.text: Don't get stuck on perfectionism. 'Good enough' is your motto.

ted_talks.text: Watch TED talks. The speakers have great delivery and clear structure.

language_math.text: Look for patterns. Language is a mathematical system of symbols.

childhood_recall.text: Remember how you learned your native language: you listened a lot and weren't afraid to fail.

physics_change.text: Neurogenesis is possible! Every new word literally changes your brain's physics.

single_task.text: Use the single-task method. First only grammar, then only words.

air_writing.text: Visualize writing a word in the air with your finger.

subs_off.text: Turn off subtitles as soon as you understand at least 30% of the speech.

humor_empathy.text: Try to understand native humor. This is the highest level of fluency.

sparring_partner.text: Find someone at your level. Progress goes faster together.

foundation_rules.text: Learn the alphabet and reading rules immediately. A wrong foundation is hard to fix later.

sleep_8h.text: 8 hours of sleep isn't a luxury, it's brain maintenance.

boring_book.text: If a book is boring in your native language, don't read it in a foreign one.

anchor_knowledge.text: Attach new knowledge to something you already know for sure.

path_enjoy.text: Enjoy the process rather than just waiting for the end result.

clarity_short.text: Write short sentences. Conciseness is a sign of language control.

ergonomics.text: An uncomfortable chair steals your attention. Get comfortable.

skill_not_gift.text: Language ability is a trained skill, not a born gift.

familiar_series.text: Watch familiar shows. You already know the plot, so the brain focuses on the speech.

karaoke.text: Sing songs in the language. This trains breathing and speech flow.

timing_best.text: Best time for memory is an hour after waking up or an hour before bed.

carrot_vision.text: Imagine the opportunities the language will open. The brain needs a carrot.

brain_energy.text: The brain consumes 20% of your body's energy. Don't study hungry.

sentence_builder.text: Use sentence builders. Assemble a phrase from different blocks.

digital_detox.text: A digital detox once a week restores mental sharpness.

idiom_spice.text: Study idioms — they make your speech 'tasty' and natural.

game_dopamine.text: Make learning a game. Alternate difficult tasks with very easy ones.

rem_sleep.text: Reviewing words before bed triggers their processing during REM sleep.

dialects.text: Listen to different dialects. This expands your brain's acoustic range.

wall_immersion.text: Surround yourself with the language. Posters, radio, books should be visible.

conjunctions.text: Use conjunctions. They are the glue that turns words into coherent speech.

neck_massage.text: Neck massage improves blood flow to the head and cognitive function.

volume_range.text: Read out loud at different volumes — from a whisper to a shout.

no_guilt.text: Don't blame yourself for missing a day. Just get back to it the next day.

project_goal.text: Set a goal: write an article or a post in the language in a month.

unique_key.text: Try different methods. Your brain is unique, find your own 'key'.

speed_grad.text: First slow and correct, then fast. Don't rush your pronunciation.

episodic_mem.text: Episodic memory is stronger than semantic. Learn through events.

cat_explain.text: Explain grammar to your cat or a stuffed animal.

screenshot_list.text: See an interesting word online? Take a screenshot, analyze it later.

battery_change.text: Changing activities (language -> math -> sport) is the best rest.

cold_water.text: Washing your face with cold water activates the vagus nerve and alerts you.

polysemy.text: The word 'apple' is both a fruit and a company. Learn multiple meanings.

intermediate_plateau.text: Don't get stuck at the Intermediate level. Dive into specific topics.

leitner_system.text: Leitner System: a box-based system for flashcards with intervals.

light_quality.text: Study with good lighting to avoid straining your eyes and brain.

antioxidants.text: Antioxidants in berries protect neurons from oxidative stress.

teach_to_learn.text: Tell your friends what you've learned. Teaching is the best way to understand.

affixes.text: Suffixes and prefixes help you understand the meaning of 50% of unknown words.

permission_wrong.text: Give yourself permission to speak incorrectly. The main thing is to convey meaning.

two_min_rule_2.text: Use the 'two-minute rule' for small language tasks.

sketches.text: Draw small sketches next to new words.

drift_notice.text: Notice when your thoughts drift. Bring them back gently without self-criticism.

language_mind.text: Your native language affects your thinking. A foreign one expands it.

magnet_sentences.text: Build sentences from magnet words on the fridge.

stable_glucose.text: Avoid blood sugar spikes. Stable glucose means stable focus.

logic_math.text: Understand the language's algorithm. Every language has its own 'math'.

cartoons.text: Watch cartoons. They have exaggerated articulation and simple language.

weekly_review.text: Do a review of everything you learned once a week.

walking_audio.text: Listen to audio lessons while walking. The rhythm of steps helps the rhythm of speech.

ritual_candle.text: Light a specific candle or turn on a certain lamp only for study sessions.

face_muscles.text: Train your tongue physically. New sounds require new facial muscle movements.

synonym_chains.text: Use synonym chains: big -> huge -> gigantic.

brain_net.text: Your brain isn't a flash drive, it's a net. Weave connections, don't just store facts.

skimming.text: Try to read text as fast as possible just to catch the gist.

social_magnet.text: Surround yourself with people who are also learning languages.

micro_learning.text: Microlearning (1-2 minutes) is more effective than long lectures.

sleep_halves.text: The first half of the night is for the body, the second is for the mind and memory.

scene_breakdown.text: Analyze one movie scene until you understand every single word.

no_mental_trans.text: Don't translate in your head. Try to link the word directly to the object.

collocations.text: Learn collocations. Not 'do a photo', but 'take a photo'.

effort_reward.text: The more effort spent recalling, the stronger the neural connection.

mindful_notice.text: Notice foreign words in signs, menus, and songs around you.

tab_hygiene.text: Close all unnecessary browser tabs. Each tab is an attention leak.

peak_start.text: Do the hardest thing in the first 15 minutes of your session.

support_comm.text: Find a supportive community or teacher. Approval is important for the brain.

target_radio.text: Listen to radio from the country of the target language to immerse yourself.

ten_verbs.text: Learn 10 basic verbs in all tenses — they are the foundation.

prepositions.text: Learn prepositions together with verbs. They are inseparable.

choline_eggs.text: Eggs contain choline, which is necessary for acetylcholine synthesis in the brain.

self_talk.text: Talk to yourself. Comment on your actions in the target language.

frank_method.text: Read adapted books using the Ilya Frank method.

forest_study.text: Try the 'forest bathing' technique — studying in the fresh air.

break_down_goal.text: Break down 'learn a language' into 'understand memes' or 'order pizza'.

emotion_engine.text: Fear and boredom are the enemies of memory. Make learning exciting.

regular_tests.text: Take tests regularly. Not for a grade, but to check for gaps.

evening_walk.text: Evening walks help you 'digest' information received during the day.

social_reward.text: Delete social media during intense study. Bring it back as a reward.

five_elements.text: Group information in 3-5 elements. The brain struggles with more.

tone_pitch.text: Watch your intonation. In some languages, it changes the word's meaning.

bad_fluent.text: It's better to speak poorly than to stay silent perfectly.

night_repeat.text: If you can't sleep, review your word list. It's relaxing and useful.

hormones.text: Testosterone and estrogen affect verbal abilities. Monitor your health.

room_per_lang.text: Use different rooms for different languages or topics.

staring_pause.text: Staring at one point after studying helps neurons connect.

regularity_key.text: The main secret is regularity. The brain loves predictable loads.
